# docs/memory/waf/

<!-- Generated by php tools/memory_index.php, except the key rules between the two marker lines, which are written by hand. -->

Firewall (waf.php): rules, bans, rate limits, bots, logs, security headers.

## Key rules

<!-- key-rules:start -->
- Keep `waf.php`, `includes/geo.php` and `includes/db_guard.php` free of `functions.php`, `lang()`, sessions and HTTP calls: `router.php` runs them first (`waf-architecture-and-phases.md`).
- Keep signature scanning in the init phase and the `waf_run()` body fail-open in its try/catch: a firewall that breaks a request is worse than none (`waf-architecture-and-phases.md`).
- Never reorder the bot classification: attack tools first, the operator's Blocked Bots after the built-in lists, residual signal last (`waf-score-calibration-and-bot-order.md`).
- Exempt by path (robots.txt, `.well-known/`) or by running script (`health.php`), never by query string; they skip the bot policy, never the IP list or rate limits (`waf-path-exemption-and-robots.md`).
- Take the visitor's address only from `waf_client_ip()` and count per `waf_ip_subject()` (the /64 for IPv6); never copy the proxy logic (`waf-ip-subject-ipv6-64.md`).
- Refuse only through `waf_deny()`, whose mode check keeps Monitor mode's promise; only the operator's IP list blocks in every mode (`waf-kill-switch-and-monitor-mode.md`).
- Give every endpoint that accepts a password `pg_login_throttle_guard()` and `pg_login_record_failure()`; the throttle works with the firewall off (`waf-login-throttle.md`).
- Log every new limit or gate with `waf_log_event()` and every new deny path in `data/firewall.log`; a protection that refuses silently is half a protection (`waf-fail2ban-log.md`).
- Write a new IP column as `VARCHAR(45)` and a ban as one atomic `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` (`waf-ipv6-ban-column-width.md`).
- Count aggregated log rows with `SUM(hit_count)`, never `COUNT(*)`, and cap the table with `MAX(id)` (`waf-log-aggregation-and-cap.md`).
- Send a visitor to a sign-in screen only for a page opening: `get_file.php` goes through `get_file_sign_in_redirect()`, which answers a sub-resource fetch (`waf_fetch_is_subresource()`) with 403, and such a fetch of a sign-in screen is not counted on the sensitive allowance (`waf-subresource-sign-in-fetches.md`).
- Register a rate refusal with the burst flag (`waf_register_offence($ip, $score, $blocking, true)`: one offence per subject and minute) and a signature hit, an attack tool or a wrong key without it; a `concurrent` refusal registers none and a rate ban never climbs the ladder (`waf-ban-ladder.md`); never auto-ban an address staff signed in from (`waf-offence-fold-and-staff-address.md`).
- Gate a new per-address counter or ban on `waf_ip_is_counted()` (not infrastructure, not a private or reserved address; the lists still apply), and go by `waf_script_name()`, never `basename(SCRIPT_NAME)`: the web root's `index.php` is the router (`waf-counter-subjects-and-endpoints.md`).
- Never send mail or touch `functions.php` from `waf.php`: queue the operator's ban notice with `waf_ban_notice_queue()`; `pg_waf_ban_notice_send()` mails it after `waf_run('init')` (`waf-ban-notice.md`).
- Serve nothing to a banned address, token or not: the rescue is the command-line `waf_unban.php`, and a Settings save whose block entries cover the operator's own address is refused (`waf-self-rescue.md`).
<!-- key-rules:end -->

## Files

- `INDEX.md` lists the 39 files of this folder, one line each: search it rather than read it whole, then open only the files that match.
- `grep -i 'word' docs/memory/waf/INDEX.md`; across every folder: `grep -i 'word' docs/memory/*/INDEX.md`.
